title: Spain's transport minister offers his resignation after last week's deadly train crash
summary: After two deadly train crashes this year, Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente has said he will step down.

image.caption: Spain has seen two deadly train accidents this year [FILE: Feb 3, 2026]Image: Alberto Ortega/Europa Press/IMAGO

blocks.text: Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente offered his resignation on Tuesday in the wake of a train crash on October 28 south of Madrid that killed 69 people.

The tragedy, Spain's second fatal rail collision in less than a year, has intensified scrutiny of railway safety and added political pressure on Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez ahead of parliamentary elections on November 29
"A transport ​minister ‌in a country like Spain cannot continue in ‌office with two accidents ‌of ​this severity in less than a year," he told lawmakers.
Puente did not specify when he will leave ​his post.
